text.text_excerpt: If there is only one place I could suggest you eat in New Orleans, it would be Port of Call. Maybe it's because I prefer burgers to seafood, but maybe it's because the burger here is that good. I love that this place is a total dive, it's pretty much a bar with burgers. The menu is not very extensive (not that it needs to be) but maybe that's why they do what they do so well. Burgers with loaded baked potatoes and giant cocktails. This place is small and it's not fast food so be prepared for a wait unless you can snag a spot at the bar but it's well worth your wait. The service here isn't going to win any awards any time soon but eh, it gives this place that much more character. Go there.

Well, this is cool that my first restaurant review after moving to New Orleans a few weeks ago gets to be for a great restaurant and a fantastic meal. let me start by saying I'm a restaurant manager. I managed 2 of the best places in Northern New Jersey for a number of years, so if I say this place is the real deal? Trust me. It's the titties. As we happened to drive by the Port of Call, my one NOLa friend said, "Oh, they have good burgers. Are you hungry?". Really? when is a man NOT hungry for a good burger? A man can finish a 2 hour Thanksgiving dinner and if someone says, "Wanna go get a burger?" he'll respond, "HELL YEAH!!". After a spot on prediction of a 10 minute wait by the awesom...

Port of Call has been said to have the "Best Burger in New Orleans". That was enough to get me to hunt it down. Well, it's a little hole-in-the-wall kind of burger joint/bar. It was dark inside and had a very relaxed & casual "homey" feel to it, like your typical neighborhood bar. The 1/2 pound burgers are made to order and have a baked potato on the side, which I LOVE WAY more than french fries, personally. The burger was great and juicy and def tantalized the taste buds. At $10 & change for a cheeseburger stacked high with cheddar, it's not exactly cheap, but it's def worth the cost! I don't know about being the "Best in NOLA", but it's pretty freakin' good.
